html:
The Roanoke were a Carolina Algonquian people of Roanoke Island and the nearby mainland of North Carolina. They are remembered because the first English colony in America was planted in their country.

In 1584 an expedition sent by Walter Raleigh met their chief Wingina and took two men, Wanchese of Roanoke and Manteo of the Croatan, to England. The next year the Roanoke colony arrived. Relations soured over food, and in 1586 the colony's governor Ralph Lane had Wingina killed. The artist John White drew the villages and people of the region in watercolours that are still the best pictures of coastal Algonquian life. A second colony in 1587 vanished, the "Lost Colony". Epidemics and wars with later settlers broke up the Roanoke, and their survivors merged with neighbours such as the Pamlico.
